what_this_tests: Pick the right identity: IAM role, IAM user, or federated identity. Roles win by default.
SCPs cap permissions in member accounts. They never grant, and they skip the management account.
IAM roles and STS issue temporary credentials for EC2 instance profiles and cross-account access.
Identity-based policies attach to users and roles. Resource-based policies attach to S3 buckets, KMS keys, and role trust policies.

signal_words.phrase: no long-term credentials
guardrail across member accounts
workforce federation into multiple accounts
signal_words.points_to: AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO)

signal_words.phrase: app users sign in with Google or Apple
another AWS account needs this bucket
signal_words.points_to: S3 bucket policy or cross-account IAM role

core_services.name: IAM
core_services.job: Controls who is authenticated and what they are authorized to do in an AWS account.
core_services.choose_when: You grant API permissions to users, groups, or roles inside one account.
core_services.avoid_when: You need a permissions ceiling across every account in an organization. Add SCPs.
core_services.trap_words: root user, long-term access keys
core_services.aws_official_description: IAM securely controls access to AWS resources. It governs who is authenticated (signed in) and authorized (has permissions) to use them.
verified_claims: IAM, IAM Identity Center, and AWS STS carry no additional charge.
IAM is eventually consistent. AWS says keep IAM changes out of high-availability code paths.
IAM roles have no password or access keys. Assuming one returns temporary credentials.

core_services.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
core_services.job: Federates workforce users into multiple AWS accounts and AWS managed applications from one place.
core_services.choose_when: Employees need SSO and permission sets across accounts, often synced from an external IdP.
core_services.avoid_when: The users are your app's customers. Use Amazon Cognito.
core_services.trap_words: customer identities, mobile app users, AWS SSO
core_services.aws_official_description: IAM Identity Center connects workforce users to AWS accounts and AWS managed applications. It syncs users from your existing identity provider or manages them directly.
verified_claims: AWS Single Sign-On was renamed AWS IAM Identity Center on July 26, 2022. The sso and identitystore API namespaces are unchanged.
Multi-account permissions require an organization instance, deployed in the Organizations management account.

core_services.name: AWS Organizations SCPs
core_services.job: Caps the maximum permissions IAM users and roles in member accounts can use.
core_services.choose_when: You must block an action in every member account, including that account's root user.
core_services.avoid_when: You need to grant access. SCPs only subtract.
core_services.trap_words: granting access, management account, service-linked roles
core_services.aws_official_description: SCPs are organization policies that set the maximum available permissions for IAM users and roles in an organization.
verified_claims: AWS states plainly: 'No permissions are granted by an SCP.' Effective permissions are the intersection of SCP and IAM policy.
SCPs affect member accounts only, including each member root user. They have no effect in the management account.
SCPs do not restrict service-linked roles. SCPs require all features enabled in the organization.

core_services.name: Amazon Cognito
core_services.job: User directory, authentication server, and credential broker for web and mobile app users.
core_services.choose_when: Your app needs sign-up, sign-in, and federation with Google, Apple, Facebook, SAML, or OIDC.
core_services.avoid_when: Employees need console or CLI access across accounts. Use IAM Identity Center.
core_services.trap_words: workforce SSO, permission sets, AWS console access
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon Cognito is an identity platform for web and mobile apps: a user directory, an authentication server, and an authorization service for OAuth 2.0 tokens and AWS credentials.
verified_claims: User pools issue OAuth 2.0 and OIDC JWTs. Identity pools exchange trusted claims for temporary AWS credentials from STS.
Identity pools can issue limited-access credentials to unauthenticated guest users.
Identity pools support role-based and attribute-based access control via principal tags.

comparisons: IAM role vs IAM user: roles yield temporary credentials and are the default. AWS reserves users for cases federation cannot cover, such as legacy tools and emergency access.
IAM Identity Center vs Cognito: Identity Center is workforce into AWS. Cognito is customers into your app.
SCP vs IAM policy: SCPs cap. IAM policies grant. Both must allow the action.
exam_moves: Block an action org-wide, even for a member root user: SCP. SCPs do not touch the management account or service-linked roles.
EC2 calling AWS APIs: attach an IAM role via instance profile. Never store access keys on the instance.
Anonymous public read of S3 objects needs a bucket policy with "Principal": "*". Identity policies cannot name anonymous callers.
Cross-account DynamoDB access: role in the owning account, trust policy naming the other account, sts:AssumeRole from there.

what_this_tests: Choose KMS vs CloudHSM. The split is tenancy and control, not FIPS level.
Secrets Manager rotates on a schedule. Parameter Store does not rotate at all.
Macie finds sensitive data and public buckets in S3. Nothing else does.
S3 encrypts every new object by default with SSE-S3. SSE-KMS adds key policies and CloudTrail visibility.

signal_words.phrase: rotate database credentials on a schedule
find PII or PHI in S3
single-tenant HSM under my control
config strings at no additional charge
encrypt at rest, no code change

core_services.name: AWS KMS
core_services.job: Creates and controls symmetric and asymmetric keys used across AWS services.
core_services.choose_when: You encrypt S3, EBS, RDS, and more with key policies and CloudTrail auditing.
core_services.avoid_when: You need single-tenant HSMs you administer outside IAM. Use CloudHSM.
core_services.trap_words: single-tenant, exclusive HSM control, PKCS #11
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS KMS is a managed service for creating and controlling the keys that encrypt and sign your data. KMS keys are protected by FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3 validated HSMs.
verified_claims: KMS keys sit in FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3 validated HSMs. FIPS Level 3 alone no longer separates KMS from CloudHSM.
KMS keys never leave the service unencrypted.
AWS KMS is backed by a published service level agreement.

core_services.name: AWS CloudHSM
core_services.job: Gives you single-tenant, general-purpose HSMs in AWS that you administer yourself.
core_services.choose_when: You need full control of keys and algorithms, or a PKCS #11 / JCE / CNG / KSP app moved to the cloud.
core_services.avoid_when: The question says least operational overhead. Use KMS.
core_services.trap_words: managed keys, low operational overhead, native S3/EBS integration
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS CloudHSM gives you complete control over high-availability hardware security modules in the AWS Cloud, with automated backups, provisioning, and maintenance.
verified_claims: CloudHSM HSMs are general purpose and single tenant. FIPS-mode clusters are FIPS 140-2 level-3 or FIPS 140-3 level-3 validated.
CloudHSM also offers non-FIPS mode clusters for use cases outside those validations.
The CloudHSM data plane is end-to-end encrypted and invisible to AWS. You manage HSM users outside IAM.

core_services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
core_services.job: Stores, retrieves, and rotates database credentials, API keys, and OAuth tokens.
core_services.choose_when: Secrets must be fetched at runtime and rotated on a schedule.
core_services.avoid_when: The data is non-secret config and you want no per-secret monthly charge.
core_services.trap_words: free storage, plain config strings
core_services.aws_official_description: Secrets Manager manages, retrieves, and rotates database credentials, application credentials, OAuth tokens, and API keys across their lifecycle, on an automatic rotation schedule.
verified_claims: Billing is per secret per month plus per API call. Secrets marked for deletion are free.
Non-managed rotation runs a Lambda function, billed at Lambda rates.
Encryption with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager is free. A customer managed key is billed at KMS rates.

core_services.name: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
core_services.job: Stores hierarchical config as String, StringList, and KMS-encrypted SecureString parameters.
core_services.choose_when: You need cheap, versioned config for EC2, Lambda, ECS, CodeBuild, or CloudFormation.
core_services.avoid_when: You need rotation or native database integration. Use Secrets Manager.
core_services.trap_words: automatic password rotation, native RDS rotation
core_services.aws_official_description: Parameter Store is a centralized store for named configuration values, with secure storage, hierarchy, and versioning at scale.
verified_claims: AWS lists Parameter Store credential rotation as 'None'. Secrets Manager is 'Automatic, with native database integrations'.
Standard tier: 10,000 parameters per account per Region, 4 KB max value, no additional charge.
Advanced tier: 100,000 parameters, 8 KB max value, billed. Parameter Store keeps the 100 most recent versions.

core_services.name: Amazon Macie
core_services.job: Finds sensitive data in Amazon S3 and flags buckets with security or access-control risk.
core_services.choose_when: You must locate PII, financial data, or credentials in S3 and catch public buckets.
core_services.avoid_when: You need CVE scanning (Inspector) or log-based threat detection (GuardDuty).
core_services.trap_words: EC2 scanning, network threats, non-S3 data stores
core_services.aws_official_description: Macie is a data security service that discovers sensitive data using machine learning and pattern matching, and surfaces data security risks.
verified_claims: Macie's scope is S3. It inventories S3 general purpose buckets and monitors them for security and access control.
Two discovery modes: automated sensitive data discovery (continuous sampling) and sensitive data discovery jobs (targeted).
Detection uses managed data identifiers plus custom regex identifiers. Findings publish to EventBridge and Security Hub.

core_services.name: S3 Server-Side Encryption (SSE)
core_services.job: Encrypts objects as S3 writes them to disk and decrypts on authorized read.
core_services.choose_when: Data at rest in S3 must be encrypted transparently. SSE-KMS when you need key policies and CloudTrail.
core_services.avoid_when: Data must be encrypted before it leaves your environment. Use client-side encryption.
core_services.trap_words: in-transit encryption, client-side encryption
core_services.aws_official_description: Server-side encryption is encryption at the destination. S3 encrypts data at the object level as it writes to disk and decrypts it on access.
verified_claims: Since January 5, 2023, every new S3 object upload is encrypted automatically at no cost. SSE-S3 is the default for every bucket.
Four mutually exclusive options: SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, DSSE-KMS (two AES-256 layers), SSE-C.
SSE-S3 uses a unique 256-bit AES key per object, itself encrypted by a regularly rotated root key.

comparisons: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: Secrets Manager rotates automatically and bills per secret per month. Parameter Store standard tier is free, stores SecureString, and rotates nothing.
KMS vs CloudHSM: both use FIPS Level 3 HSMs. KMS is multi-tenant and integrated. CloudHSM is single-tenant, invisible to AWS, and managed by you.
Macie vs GuardDuty: Macie inspects data in S3. GuardDuty inspects CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs for behavior.
exam_moves: 'Least operational overhead' plus encryption keys means KMS. Pick CloudHSM only for single-tenant or exclusive control.
Rotating RDS passwords on a schedule is Secrets Manager, never Parameter Store.
Discovering PII in S3 and public buckets is Amazon Macie.
S3 is already SSE-S3 encrypted by default. Move to SSE-KMS when the question wants customer managed keys or CloudTrail key usage.

what_this_tests: Security groups are stateful and allow-only. NACLs are stateless, numbered, and support deny.
WAF handles Layer 7 exploits. Shield handles DDoS.
Network Firewall does Suricata IPS and domain filtering at the VPC perimeter.

signal_words.phrase: stateful firewall on an instance or ENI
explicit deny of an IP at the subnet
SQL injection or XSS
DDoS cost protection, Shield Response Team
deep packet inspection, domain filtering

core_services.name: Security Groups
core_services.job: Stateful firewall on the resources (ENIs) it is associated with.
core_services.choose_when: You control which protocols, ports, and sources reach an EC2 instance, ALB, or RDS instance.
core_services.avoid_when: You need an explicit deny or subnet-wide blocking. Use a NACL.
core_services.trap_words: explicit deny, subnet-level, stateless
core_services.aws_official_description: A security group controls the traffic allowed to reach and leave the resources it is associated with. Only traffic allowed by its rules reaches the instance.
verified_claims: Security groups are stateful. Response traffic is allowed regardless of the opposite-direction rules.
Security groups hold allow rules only. There is no deny rule.
No charge for security groups. One resource can have multiple security groups.

core_services.name: Network ACLs (NACLs)
core_services.job: Allows or denies inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level, statelessly.
core_services.choose_when: You must explicitly deny an IP or CIDR for a whole subnet.
core_services.avoid_when: You want return traffic allowed automatically. Use a security group.
core_services.trap_words: stateful, instance-level, automatic return traffic
core_services.aws_official_description: A network ACL allows or denies specific inbound or outbound traffic at the subnet level.
verified_claims: Rules are numbered 1 to 32766 and evaluated lowest first. The first match applies and evaluation stops.
NACLs are stateless. Responses need matching outbound ephemeral-port rules.
Every subnet maps to exactly one NACL, defaulting to the VPC default NACL. No charge.

core_services.name: AWS WAF
core_services.job: Filters HTTP(S) requests to protected web resources using rules you define.
core_services.choose_when: You block SQL injection, XSS, bots, or rate-limit in front of CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, or AppSync.
core_services.avoid_when: The attack is a Layer 3/4 flood, or the traffic is not HTTP.
core_services.trap_words: UDP, Network Load Balancer, direct EC2 attachment
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that monitors HTTP(S) requests to protected resources and returns the content, HTTP 403, or a custom response.
verified_claims: Protected resource types: CloudFront distribution, API Gateway REST API, Application Load Balancer, AppSync GraphQL API, Cognito user pool, App Runner service, Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, Verified Access instance, AWS Amplify.
No direct attachment to EC2 or an NLB. ECS is protected via a WAF-enabled Application Load Balancer.

core_services.name: AWS Shield Advanced
core_services.job: Expanded DDoS protection with cost protection and Shield Response Team escalation.
core_services.choose_when: Critical internet-facing apps need higher DDoS protection and billing protection during attacks.
core_services.avoid_when: Shield Standard, included free for all customers, already covers you.
core_services.trap_words: free tier, Layer 7 rule authoring, internal VPC traffic
core_services.aws_official_description: Shield Advanced is a managed service protecting applications against DDoS attacks, volumetric bots, and vulnerability exploitation, with expanded protection for the resources you enroll.
verified_claims: $3,000 per month per organization plus data transfer fees.
The subscription covers standard AWS WAF costs on protected resources: per web ACL, per rule, and base per-million-request inspection.
DDoS cost protection covers scaling spikes on protected EC2, ELB, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, and Route 53. SRT engagement requires Business or Enterprise Support.

core_services.name: AWS Network Firewall
core_services.job: Managed stateful firewall and IDS/IPS at the VPC perimeter.
core_services.choose_when: You need deep packet inspection, domain allow/deny lists, or Suricata IPS rules on VPC traffic.
core_services.avoid_when: Per-instance port filtering is enough, or you need HTTP payload rules. Use security groups or WAF.
core_services.trap_words: Layer 7 web ACL, SQL injection rules, per-instance firewall
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Network Firewall is a stateful managed network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for a VPC. It filters traffic at the VPC perimeter, including traffic via internet gateway, NAT gateway, VPN, or Direct Connect.
verified_claims: Stateful inspection uses Suricata and supports Suricata-compatible rules. Stateless rule groups inspect single packets.
Firewall endpoints live in dedicated firewall subnets. An endpoint cannot filter traffic for its own subnet.
AWS Firewall Manager centrally configures Network Firewall across accounts in AWS Organizations.

comparisons: Security groups vs NACLs: stateful, allow-only, per-ENI versus stateless, allow-and-deny, numbered, per-subnet.
WAF vs Shield: WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests. Shield mitigates DDoS. Standard is free; Advanced adds cost protection and SRT.
Network Firewall vs security groups: Suricata IDS/IPS at the VPC edge versus per-resource port and source allow-lists.
exam_moves: Explicit deny of one IP requires a NACL. Security groups have no deny rule.
Security group inbound 80 allows the response automatically. A NACL needs an outbound ephemeral-port rule. NAT gateways use ports 1024-65535.
WAF attaches to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway REST, AppSync, Cognito user pools, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify. Never to EC2 or an NLB.
DDoS cost protection on EC2, ELB, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, and Route 53 is Shield Advanced only.

what_this_tests: CloudTrail records API calls. Config records resource state and compliance.
GuardDuty detects behavior from logs. Inspector scans for CVEs.
X-Ray traces requests across services. Logs Insights queries log text.

signal_words.phrase: who made this API call
cryptomining or compromised credentials
unpatched CVEs on EC2, ECR images, Lambda
configuration history and compliance rules
latency across microservices

core_services.name: AWS CloudTrail
core_services.job: Records actions by users, roles, and AWS services as auditable events.
core_services.choose_when: You need who did what, to which resource, and when, from console, CLI, SDK, or API.
core_services.avoid_when: You need CPU or performance metrics. Use CloudWatch.
core_services.trap_words: CPU metrics, intrusion prevention, configuration state
core_services.aws_official_description: CloudTrail enables operational and risk auditing, governance, and compliance. Actions taken by a user, role, or AWS service are recorded as events.
verified_claims: Event history covers the past 90 days of management events per Region, searchable and free.
Longer retention needs a trail to S3 (one copy of ongoing management events free from CloudTrail) or CloudTrail Lake.
CloudTrail Lake retains events up to 3,653 days (about 10 years) on the one-year extendable pricing option.

core_services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
core_services.job: Analyzes AWS logs with threat intelligence and ML to flag suspicious activity.
core_services.choose_when: You want agentless threat detection for compromised credentials, cryptomining, or exfiltration.
core_services.avoid_when: You need CVE inventories on hosts or images. Use Inspector.
core_services.trap_words: vulnerability scanning, patch compliance, rule-based firewall
core_services.aws_official_description: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors and analyzes AWS data sources and logs, using threat intelligence feeds and machine learning models.
verified_claims: Foundational data sources, ingested automatically: CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, DNS logs.
Optional protection plans add S3 data events, EKS audit logs, RDS login activity, EBS malware scanning, Runtime Monitoring, and Lambda network activity.
30-day free trial. Manageable org-wide through AWS Organizations.

core_services.name: AWS Security Hub
core_services.job: Aggregates security findings and checks accounts against security standards from one place.
core_services.choose_when: You need a central security posture view across accounts, Regions, AWS services, and partner tools.
core_services.avoid_when: You need live threat detection, vulnerability scanning, or API audit history. Use GuardDuty, Inspector, or CloudTrail.
core_services.trap_words: vulnerability scanning, behavioral threat detection, API audit log, packet firewall
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Security Hub gives you a comprehensive view of your security state in AWS and helps you check your environment against security industry standards and best practices.
verified_claims: Security Hub collects findings from AWS services, supported third-party products, and custom integrations.
Security standards run automated checks and produce findings for failed controls.
Organizations can manage Security Hub across accounts with a delegated administrator.

core_services.name: Amazon Inspector
core_services.job: Discovers workloads and continually scans them for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
core_services.choose_when: You need continuous CVE assessment of EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions.
core_services.avoid_when: You need live behavioral detection (GuardDuty) or API audit trails (CloudTrail).
core_services.trap_words: API auditing, behavioral detection, S3 data scanning
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management service that automatically discovers workloads and continually scans EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
verified_claims: No scan scheduling. Inspector rescans on package install, patch, or newly published CVE affecting the resource.
Inspector risk score is CVSS-format and adjusts the NVD base score for your environment, for example when no open network path exists.
Org-wide activation via a delegated administrator. Findings publish to EventBridge and Security Hub.

core_services.name: AWS Config
core_services.job: Records resource configuration over time and evaluates it against rules.
core_services.choose_when: You need configuration history, relationships, compliance rules, conformance packs, or auto-remediation.
core_services.avoid_when: You need the identity behind the change. Use CloudTrail.
core_services.trap_words: API call history, threat detection, performance metrics
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Config gives a detailed view of AWS resource configurations, how resources relate, and how they were configured in the past.
verified_claims: Config rules evaluate resources continuously as they are created, changed, or deleted, and flag noncompliance with a notification.
Conformance packs deploy rule collections as one entity. Remediation actions fix noncompliant resources.
Aggregators give multi-account, multi-Region views. Snapshots and history land in S3; notifications go to SNS.

core_services.name: AWS X-Ray
core_services.job: Collects trace data per request and builds a trace map across services.
core_services.choose_when: You must see where time is spent across API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, and downstream calls.
core_services.avoid_when: You only need to search log text. Use Logs Insights.
core_services.trap_words: security auditing, packet inspection, log aggregation
core_services.aws_official_description: X-Ray collects data about requests your application serves and provides tools to view, filter, and analyze it to identify issues and optimization opportunities.
verified_claims: The trace map shows client, front-end service, and backends, used to find bottlenecks and latency spikes.
SDKs send JSON segment documents over UDP to the X-Ray daemon, which batches uploads. The daemon ships with Elastic Beanstalk and Lambda.

core_services.name: CloudWatch Logs Insights
core_services.job: Interactively queries and analyzes log data in CloudWatch Logs.
core_services.choose_when: You troubleshoot using application logs, VPC flow logs, or CloudTrail logs.
core_services.avoid_when: You need one request's path and timing across services. Use X-Ray.
core_services.trap_words: distributed tracing, service map, profiling
core_services.aws_official_description: CloudWatch Logs Insights interactively searches and analyzes log data in CloudWatch Logs so you can respond to operational issues.
verified_claims: Three query languages: Logs Insights QL, OpenSearch PPL, and OpenSearch SQL.
Queries time out after 60 minutes. Results stay available for seven days.
Billing is by uncompressed log data scanned. Fields auto-discover for Route 53, Lambda, CloudTrail, VPC, and JSON logs.

comparisons: CloudTrail vs CloudWatch: CloudTrail is who did what, when. CloudWatch is how the system behaves.
GuardDuty vs Inspector: GuardDuty reads CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs for active behavior. Inspector scans EC2, ECR images, and Lambda for CVEs.
Config vs CloudTrail: Config stores the resource state and its compliance. CloudTrail stores the API call that changed it.
exam_moves: Who terminated that EC2 instance last week: CloudTrail. Event history is only 90 days, so a trail or Lake is needed beyond that.
Agentless threat detection from CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs: GuardDuty.
Slow API Gateway plus Lambda plus DynamoDB app: X-Ray trace map isolates the segment.
Prove no S3 bucket is public, continuously: AWS Config rules with remediation.

what_this_tests: Private subnets reach the internet outbound only, through a NAT gateway in a public subnet.
A subnet is public only if its route table points at an internet gateway.
Elastic IPs persist and remap. Auto-assigned public IPv4 addresses change on stop/start.

signal_words.phrase: private instances must download patches
signal_words.points_to: NAT gateway in a public subnet

signal_words.phrase: internet clients reach the web server
signal_words.points_to: Internet gateway plus a public IPv4 address

signal_words.phrase: fixed public IP for an allow-list
route 0.0.0.0/0 out of the subnet
signal_words.points_to: Route table to IGW (public) or NAT gateway (private)

signal_words.phrase: port forwarding or bastion on the NAT device

core_services.name: Amazon VPC
core_services.job: Provides a logically isolated virtual network where AWS resources launch with controlled IP ranges and routing.
core_services.choose_when: You need to design CIDR blocks, public and private tiers, routing, gateways, and network boundaries for workloads.
core_services.avoid_when: You only need an AWS-managed public service endpoint, or you need account-level identity controls instead of network isolation.
core_services.trap_words: CIDR range, isolated network, public subnet, private subnet, route table, internet gateway
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) gives you full control over your virtual networking environment, including resource placement, connectivity, and security.
verified_claims: A VPC is scoped to one AWS Region and can span multiple Availability Zones through its subnets.
You choose IPv4 CIDR blocks and can add IPv6 CIDR blocks for VPC addressing.
Route tables, gateways, security groups, and network ACLs control how resources communicate.

core_services.name: VPC subnets
core_services.job: Divides a VPC IP range into Availability Zone-scoped networks where resources are placed.
core_services.choose_when: You need public and private tiers, Multi-AZ placement, or routing differences for groups of resources.
core_services.avoid_when: You need a separate Region-level network boundary. Use another VPC or Region design instead.
core_services.trap_words: public subnet, private subnet, route table association, Availability Zone, NAT gateway placement
core_services.aws_official_description: A subnet is a range of IP addresses in your VPC. You launch AWS resources into a specified subnet.
verified_claims: Each subnet resides entirely within one Availability Zone.
A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway; a private subnet does not.
Subnets use route table associations to decide where traffic is directed.

core_services.name: Internet Gateway (IGW)
core_services.job: Enables two-way IPv4 and IPv6 traffic between a VPC and the internet.
core_services.choose_when: Resources have public IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and their route table points at the IGW.
core_services.avoid_when: Instances must be outbound-only. Use a NAT gateway.
core_services.trap_words: private subnets, outbound-only, bandwidth bottleneck
core_services.aws_official_description: An internet gateway is a horizontally scaled, redundant, highly available VPC component allowing communication between your VPC and the internet. It supports IPv4 and IPv6 and adds no availability risk or bandwidth constraint.
verified_claims: A subnet is public if its route table has a route to an internet gateway, private if it does not.
For IPv4 the IGW performs one-to-one NAT between the private address and the public or Elastic IP.
No charge for the internet gateway. EC2 data transfer charges still apply.

core_services.name: NAT Gateway
core_services.job: Lets private-subnet instances connect out while blocking externally initiated connections.
core_services.choose_when: Private backends need outbound patching and API calls with zero administration.
core_services.avoid_when: You need inbound access, port forwarding, or a bastion. VPC endpoints avoid NAT charges for AWS service traffic.
core_services.trap_words: inbound access, security group on the NAT gateway, port forwarding
core_services.aws_official_description: A NAT gateway lets instances in a private subnet connect to services outside the VPC, while external services cannot initiate connections to those instances.
verified_claims: 5 Gbps of bandwidth, scaling automatically to 100 Gbps. 1 million packets per second, scaling to 10 million.
Each IPv4 address supports 55,000 simultaneous connections per unique destination (IP, port, protocol). Up to 8 IPv4 addresses raise that.
Created in one Availability Zone and redundant only within it. No security group can be attached. A public NAT gateway needs an Elastic IP at creation.

core_services.name: NAT Instance
core_services.job: A customer-managed EC2 instance performing NAT for private subnets.
core_services.choose_when: You need port forwarding or a bastion on the same device.
core_services.avoid_when: You want AWS-managed availability, bandwidth, and patching. AWS recommends NAT gateways.
core_services.trap_words: fully managed, highly available by default, automatic scaling
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS recommends NAT gateways over NAT instances for better availability and bandwidth and less administration. A NAT instance runs a generic AMI configured to perform NAT.
verified_claims: AWS lists NAT instance availability as 'Use a script to manage failover between instances'. Bandwidth depends on instance type.
Port forwarding and bastion server use are supported on NAT instances and listed 'Not supported' for NAT gateways.
Security groups attach to a NAT instance but never to a NAT gateway.

core_services.name: Elastic IP (EIP)
core_services.job: Static public IPv4 address you can remap between instances or network interfaces.
core_services.choose_when: You need a stable public endpoint that survives instance replacement, or a fixed egress IP on a public NAT gateway.
core_services.avoid_when: Clients reach the workload through a load balancer or DNS name.
core_services.trap_words: dynamic public IP, private-only addressing
core_services.aws_official_description: An Elastic IP address is a static, public IPv4 address you can associate with any instance or network interface in any VPC in your account.
verified_claims: An Elastic IP masks instance failure: remap it to another instance to keep the same public endpoint.
Elastic IPs associate and disassociate programmatically and act as stable targets for external DNS records and firewall rules.

core_services.name: Route Table
core_services.job: Holds routes deciding where traffic from a subnet or gateway goes.
core_services.choose_when: You send 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway for public subnets, or to a NAT gateway for private ones.
core_services.avoid_when: You are trying to allow or deny traffic. Routing is not filtering.
core_services.trap_words: firewall rules, explicit deny, stateful inspection
core_services.aws_official_description: A route table contains routes that determine where network traffic from your subnet or gateway is directed.
verified_claims: Creating a VPC also creates its main route table. Additional route tables give per-subnet control.
Each route pairs a destination (CIDR block or prefix list) with a target such as an internet gateway, NAT gateway, peering connection, or VPN connection.

comparisons: NAT gateway vs NAT instance: managed, AZ-redundant, 5 to 100 Gbps versus self-patched EC2 with scripted failover. Only the instance does port forwarding and bastion.
IGW vs NAT gateway: IGW allows connections in both directions for public-addressed resources. NAT gateway allows only VPC-initiated connections.
Elastic IP vs auto-assigned public IPv4: the EIP belongs to your account and remaps. The auto-assigned address changes on stop/start.
exam_moves: NAT gateway goes in a PUBLIC subnet. The private subnet's 0.0.0.0/0 route points at it.
Public-subnet instance cannot reach the internet: check for a public IP and a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the IGW.
A NAT instance needs Source/Destination Check disabled on its ENI, or it drops routed packets.
A NAT gateway is redundant only inside its AZ. Deploy one per AZ and route each subnet to its local one.

what_this_tests: Reaching Amazon S3 and DynamoDB from private subnets without an internet gateway or NAT device.
Separating gateway endpoints (free, route-table based) from interface endpoints (billed, ENI based).
Knowing that gateway endpoints do not use AWS PrivateLink, while interface endpoints do.

signal_words.phrase: access S3 privately without internet
access DynamoDB privately without NAT
access SQS/KMS privately using an ENI
reach an AWS service from on-premises over Direct Connect

core_services.name: Gateway VPC Endpoint
core_services.job: Adds a route-table entry that sends S3 or DynamoDB traffic to a gateway instead of an internet gateway.
core_services.choose_when: You need S3 or DynamoDB access from a private subnet at no endpoint charge and without a NAT device.
core_services.avoid_when: You need any service other than S3 or DynamoDB, or access from a peered VPC or on-premises network.
core_services.trap_words: PrivateLink, elastic network interface, hourly cost
core_services.aws_official_description: Gateway VPC endpoints provide reliable connectivity to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device for your VPC. Gateway endpoints do not use AWS PrivateLink, unlike other types of VPC endpoints.
verified_claims: There is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints.
Gateway endpoints support only Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, and they do not use AWS PrivateLink.
AWS adds a route whose destination is an AWS-managed prefix list and whose target is the gateway endpoint.

core_services.name: Interface VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink)
core_services.job: Creates an endpoint network interface in your subnet with a private IP that fronts a PrivateLink-powered service.
core_services.choose_when: You need private access to services such as SQS, SNS, or AWS KMS, including from on-premises networks.
core_services.avoid_when: Plain S3 or DynamoDB access from inside the VPC is enough, since gateway endpoints cost nothing.
core_services.trap_words: free, route table target
core_services.aws_official_description: For each subnet that you specify from your VPC, we create an endpoint network interface in the subnet and assign it a private IP address from the subnet address range.
verified_claims: You are billed hourly usage and data processing charges for interface endpoints.
You select security groups for the endpoint network interfaces; the VPC default security group is used otherwise.
You can select only one subnet per Availability Zone for an interface endpoint.
Interface endpoints do not respond to ping requests.

comparisons: Gateway vs interface endpoint: gateway covers only S3 and DynamoDB, is free, and works through route tables. Interface endpoints cover most AWS services, bill per hour and per GB, and use endpoint network interfaces with security groups.
VPC endpoint vs NAT gateway: a NAT gateway sends traffic out to the internet. An endpoint sends traffic straight to the service without an internet gateway or NAT device.
S3 gateway vs S3 interface endpoint: Amazon S3 supports both types, so the exam distinguishes them by cost and by whether on-premises or cross-VPC access is required.
exam_moves: Cheapest private S3 or DynamoDB access from a private subnet is a gateway VPC endpoint, which carries no endpoint charge.
SQS, SNS, or AWS KMS from a private subnet requires an interface VPC endpoint, since gateway endpoints support only S3 and DynamoDB.
Gateway endpoints are configured through route tables. Interface endpoints are secured with security groups on the endpoint network interfaces.
Resources in a peered VPC cannot use your VPC's gateway endpoint to reach Amazon S3. Edge-to-edge routing is not supported.

what_this_tests: Picking a load balancer by OSI layer: ALB at layer 7, NLB at layer 4, Gateway Load Balancer at layer 3.
Matching Route 53 routing policies to failover, latency, weighted, and geolocation requirements.
Choosing CloudFront for cached HTTP content versus Global Accelerator for static anycast IP entry points.

signal_words.phrase: path-based or host-based HTTP routing
millions of requests per second, TCP/UDP
cache static content at edge locations
static anycast IP addresses for a global app
DNS-level active-passive failover
inspect traffic with third-party firewall appliances

core_services.name: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
core_services.job: Routes HTTP and HTTPS requests at OSI layer 7 using listener rules on path, host, headers, and query strings.
core_services.choose_when: You run web apps or microservices needing content-based routing to EC2, containers, IP targets, or Lambda functions.
core_services.avoid_when: You need static IPs, non-HTTP TCP or UDP protocols, or transparent appliance insertion.
core_services.trap_words: static IP, TCP, UDP, GENEVE
core_services.aws_official_description: An Application Load Balancer functions at the application layer, the seventh layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, evaluating listener rules in priority order to select a target.
verified_claims: ALB supports path conditions, host conditions, HTTP header, method, query string, and source IP conditions.
ALB can register Lambda functions as targets and IP targets outside the load balancer's VPC.
The default target group routing algorithm is round robin; least outstanding requests is also available.

core_services.name: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
core_services.job: Routes connections at OSI layer 4 and can handle millions of requests per second at very low latency.
core_services.choose_when: You need TCP, UDP, TLS, or QUIC handling, or a static IP address per enabled Availability Zone.
core_services.avoid_when: You need routing decisions based on URL paths, host headers, or other HTTP content.
core_services.trap_words: HTTP headers, path-based routing, URL inspection
core_services.aws_official_description: A Network Load Balancer functions at the fourth layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. It can handle millions of requests per second.
verified_claims: NLB target groups support the TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC protocols.
Elastic Load Balancing creates a network interface per enabled Availability Zone, giving each node a static IP address.
For an internet-facing NLB you can optionally associate one Elastic IP address per subnet.

core_services.name: Gateway Load Balancer
core_services.job: Transparently forwards all IP packets to a fleet of third-party virtual appliances using GENEVE on port 6081.
core_services.choose_when: You must send VPC traffic through firewalls, IDS/IPS, or deep packet inspection appliances before it reaches applications.
core_services.avoid_when: You are load balancing ordinary web or TCP application traffic to your own targets.
core_services.trap_words: HTTP routing, path-based rules
core_services.aws_official_description: Gateway Load Balancers enable you to deploy, scale, and manage virtual appliances, such as firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, and deep packet inspection systems.
verified_claims: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third (network) layer of the OSI model and listens for all IP packets across all ports.
It exchanges traffic with registered appliances using the GENEVE protocol on port 6081.
Gateway Load Balancer endpoints carry traffic across VPC boundaries and are set as the next hop in route tables.

core_services.name: Amazon Route 53
core_services.job: Resolves domain names and steers queries using routing policies plus health checks.
core_services.choose_when: You need DNS, active-passive failover, latency routing across Regions, or weighted traffic shifting.
core_services.avoid_when: You need content cached at edge locations or IP-layer failover faster than DNS TTLs allow.
core_services.trap_words: content caching, Layer 7 request routing
core_services.aws_official_description: When you create a record, you choose a routing policy, which determines how Amazon Route 53 responds to queries.
verified_claims: Route 53 offers simple, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, latency, IP-based, multivalue answer, and weighted routing policies.
Multivalue answer routing responds to DNS queries with up to eight healthy records selected at random.
Failover routing is used to configure active-passive failover.

core_services.name: Amazon CloudFront
core_services.job: Caches static and dynamic web content at worldwide edge locations and routes requests over the AWS backbone.
core_services.choose_when: You deliver HTTP or HTTPS content, media, or APIs to a geographically spread audience.
core_services.avoid_when: The workload is non-HTTP UDP or TCP traffic such as gaming or VoIP.
core_services.trap_words: UDP, non-HTTP protocols, static anycast IPs
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon CloudFront is a web service that speeds up distribution of your static and dynamic web content, such as .html, .css, .js, and image files, to your users through a worldwide network of data centers called edge locations.
verified_claims: By default each file stays in an edge location for 24 hours before it expires; the minimum expiration is 0 seconds.
Data transfer from AWS origins such as Amazon S3, Elastic Load Balancing, or Amazon API Gateway to CloudFront is free.
Origins can be an Amazon S3 bucket, a MediaPackage channel, or a custom HTTP server.

core_services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
core_services.job: Provides static anycast IP entry points and routes traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal endpoint.
core_services.choose_when: You need fixed IPs, fast health-based failover, or improved performance for global TCP and UDP applications.
core_services.avoid_when: Your goal is caching HTTP objects near viewers, which Global Accelerator does not do.
core_services.trap_words: caching, edge cache TTL
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Global Accelerator is a service in which you create accelerators to improve the performance of your applications for local and global users, directing traffic over the AWS global network to endpoints in the nearest Region to the client.
verified_claims: For IPv4, Global Accelerator provides two static IPv4 addresses that are anycast from the AWS edge network.
Standard accelerator endpoints can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses.
The service reacts instantly to changes in health or configuration so traffic is always directed to healthy endpoints.
Deleting an accelerator releases its static IP addresses permanently.

comparisons: ALB vs NLB: ALB works at layer 7 and routes on HTTP content. NLB works at layer 4, handles TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC, and gives a static IP per Availability Zone.
Gateway Load Balancer vs NLB: GLB works at layer 3 with GENEVE for inline appliances. NLB terminates client connections at layer 4 for your own targets.
CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: CloudFront caches HTTP content at edge locations. Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and proxies TCP/UDP over the AWS network without caching.
Route 53 latency routing vs Global Accelerator: DNS answers are cached by resolvers, so failover waits on TTL. Global Accelerator shifts traffic at the IP layer instead.
exam_moves: Need a load balancer with a static IP? Choose an NLB, or front an ALB with AWS Global Accelerator.
Routing /images to one target group and /video to another requires an ALB path condition.
To force S3 access through CloudFront, use origin access control (OAC); origin access identity (OAI) is the older mechanism.
Use Route 53 weighted routing to shift a percentage of traffic for A/B testing or blue/green cutovers.
Third-party firewall or IDS appliances inline for a VPC point to Gateway Load Balancer plus Gateway Load Balancer endpoints.

what_this_tests: Choosing Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN for hybrid connectivity based on bandwidth and encryption needs.
Using AWS Transit Gateway as a hub instead of a full mesh of VPC peering connections.
Knowing that VPC peering is non-transitive and does not allow edge-to-edge routing.

signal_words.phrase: bypass internet service providers in the network path
encrypted IPsec tunnel over the internet
hub connecting hundreds of VPCs
connect exactly two VPCs privately
share subnets across AWS accounts
branch offices talking to each other over VPN

core_services.name: AWS Direct Connect
core_services.job: Links your network to a Direct Connect location over Ethernet fiber, bypassing internet service providers.
core_services.choose_when: You need consistent bandwidth and latency, or compliance forbids traffic crossing the public internet.
core_services.avoid_when: You need connectivity within minutes or cannot wait for a physical circuit.
core_services.trap_words: internet-based, encrypted by default
core_services.aws_official_description: Direct Connect links your internal network to a Direct Connect location over a standard Ethernet fiber-optic cable, letting you create virtual interfaces directly to public AWS services or to Amazon VPC, bypassing internet service providers in your network path.
verified_claims: Direct Connect supports 1, 10, 100, and 400 Gbps optics (1000BASE-LX, 10GBASE-LR, 100GBASE-LR4, 400GBASE-LR4).
There are three virtual interface types: private, public, and transit.
Billing has two elements: port hours and outbound data transfer.
Your device must support BGP and BGP MD5 authentication, plus 802.1Q VLAN encapsulation.

core_services.name: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
core_services.job: Builds IPsec tunnels between your on-premises customer gateway device and a virtual private gateway or transit gateway.
core_services.choose_when: You need encrypted hybrid connectivity quickly and can accept internet path variability.
core_services.avoid_when: You need dedicated multi-gigabit capacity with predictable latency.
core_services.trap_words: dedicated physical connection, bypasses the internet
core_services.aws_official_description: You can enable access to your remote devices from your VPC by creating an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection and configuring routing to pass traffic through the connection. Site-to-Site VPN supports Internet Protocol security (IPsec) VPN connections.
verified_claims: Each VPN connection includes two VPN tunnels that you can use simultaneously for high availability.
Standard tunnel bandwidth is 1.25 Gbps; Large Bandwidth Tunnels support up to 5 Gbps on Transit Gateway or Cloud WAN.
Site-to-Site VPN supports IKEv2, NAT traversal, AES 256-bit encryption, and SHA-2 hashing.
A Site-to-Site VPN connection does not support Path MTU Discovery.

core_services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
core_services.job: Acts as a network transit hub interconnecting VPCs, VPNs, Direct Connect gateways, and other transit gateways.
core_services.choose_when: You have many VPCs and want central route tables instead of a peering mesh.
core_services.avoid_when: Two VPCs need to talk and peering is cheaper and simpler.
core_services.trap_words: full mesh, only two VPCs
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Transit Gateway is a network transit hub used to interconnect virtual private clouds (VPCs) and on-premises networks. All network traffic between AWS data centers is automatically encrypted at the physical layer.
verified_claims: The default quota is 5,000 attachments per transit gateway and 50 peering attachments per transit gateway.
Bandwidth per VPC attachment per Availability Zone is up to 100 Gbps in each direction.
A transit gateway supports up to 10,000 combined dynamic and static routes across all its route tables.
MTU is 8500 bytes for VPC, Direct Connect, Connect, and peering attachments, but 1500 bytes over VPN.

core_services.name: VPC peering
core_services.job: Creates a one-to-one networking connection between two VPCs routed over private IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
core_services.choose_when: Two VPCs, possibly in different accounts or Regions, need direct private connectivity.
core_services.avoid_when: You need transitive routing, overlapping CIDR blocks, or shared use of another VPC's gateways.
core_services.trap_words: transitive routing, hub and spoke
core_services.aws_official_description: A VPC peering connection is a networking connection between two VPCs that enables you to route traffic between them using private IPv4 addresses or IPv6 addresses. It is neither a gateway nor a VPN connection and does not rely on separate physical hardware.
verified_claims: There is no single point of failure for communication and no bandwidth bottleneck in a VPC peering connection.
VPC peering does not support transitive peering relationships.
You cannot create a peering connection between VPCs with matching or overlapping IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks.
Inter-Region peering traffic is encrypted before leaving AWS facilities and never traverses the public internet.

core_services.name: AWS VPN CloudHub
core_services.job: Uses one virtual private gateway as a hub so multiple Site-to-Site VPN sites can reach each other.
core_services.choose_when: You have several branch offices with internet links needing low-cost hub-and-spoke connectivity.
core_services.avoid_when: You need dedicated circuits between offices or a scalable multi-VPC router.
core_services.trap_words: dedicated high bandwidth, VPC-to-VPC routing
core_services.aws_official_description: If you have multiple AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections, you can provide secure communication between sites using the AWS VPN CloudHub. This enables your sites to communicate with each other, and not just with the resources in your VPC.
verified_claims: VPN CloudHub operates on a simple hub-and-spoke model that you can use with or without a VPC.
You must use a unique BGP ASN for each customer gateway, and the sites must not have overlapping IP ranges.
Sites connected by Direct Connect to the same virtual private gateway can also participate in VPN CloudHub.

core_services.name: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)
core_services.job: Shares resources such as VPC subnets and transit gateways with other accounts, OUs, or IAM principals.
core_services.choose_when: You want a central networking account whose subnets application accounts can launch resources into.
core_services.avoid_when: The requirement is routing traffic between separate VPCs, which needs peering or a transit gateway.
core_services.trap_words: routing traffic, copying resources
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) helps you securely share your resources across AWS accounts, within your organization or organizational units (OUs), and with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and users for supported resource types.
verified_claims: There are no additional charges for using AWS RAM or for creating resource shares.
Sharing eliminates the need to provision duplicate resources in every account.
Shared resources appear in the consuming account's native service console and API results.
Sharing with accounts outside your organization requires the recipient to accept an invitation.

comparisons: Direct Connect vs Site-to-Site VPN: Direct Connect is a dedicated fiber link that bypasses ISPs but is not encrypted by itself. Site-to-Site VPN rides the internet and is IPsec-encrypted.
Transit gateway vs VPC peering: a transit gateway is a hub supporting up to 5,000 attachments and transitive routing. Peering is strictly one-to-one and non-transitive.
Transit gateway vs VPN CloudHub: CloudHub relays branch-office traffic through one virtual private gateway. A transit gateway routes among VPCs, VPNs, and Direct Connect gateways.
VPC sharing with RAM vs peering: RAM lets accounts deploy into the same subnets. Peering connects two separate VPCs that keep their own address spaces.
exam_moves: A compliance rule that data must not traverse the public internet points to AWS Direct Connect.
VPC peering is non-transitive: A-B and A-C peerings do not let B reach C. Use a transit gateway.
Direct Connect is not encrypted on its own. Run an IPsec VPN over it, or use MACsec on supported ports.
Resources in a peered VPC cannot use the other VPC's internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, Direct Connect, or gateway endpoint.
To avoid duplicating NAT gateways in every account, share central subnets with AWS RAM.

signal_words.phrase: lowest network latency between instances
deploy app code without managing infrastructure
replicate an architecture from a template

core_services.name: Amazon EC2
core_services.job: Provides resizable virtual servers with full operating system control.
core_services.choose_when: You need root access, custom kernels or agents, or specific instance families and sizes.
core_services.avoid_when: You would rather not patch or manage servers at all.
core_services.trap_words: serverless, no operational overhead
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) provides on-demand, scalable computing capacity in the Amazon Web Services Cloud.
verified_claims: EC2 purchasing options include On-Demand Instances, Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and Dedicated Hosts.

core_services.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
core_services.job: Deploys and scales uploaded application code, handling capacity, load balancing, and health monitoring.
core_services.choose_when: A developer wants to hand over code and let AWS provision the EC2 environment.
core_services.avoid_when: You need fine-grained, declarative control over every resource in the architecture.
core_services.trap_words: infrastructure as code, granular resource control
core_services.aws_official_description: With AWS Elastic Beanstalk you can quickly deploy and manage applications in the AWS Cloud without having to learn about the infrastructure that runs those applications.
verified_claims: Elastic Beanstalk automatically handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and application health monitoring.
There is no additional charge for Elastic Beanstalk; you pay only for the underlying AWS resources.

core_services.name: EC2 Spot Instances
core_services.job: Runs workloads on spare EC2 capacity at prices below On-Demand, with the risk of interruption.
core_services.choose_when: Work is interruptible: data analysis, batch jobs, background processing, or optional tasks.
core_services.avoid_when: The workload cannot tolerate being stopped, hibernated, or terminated on short notice.
core_services.trap_words: stateful, uninterruptible, guaranteed capacity
core_services.aws_official_description: A Spot Instance is an instance that uses spare EC2 capacity that is available for less than the On-Demand price. Spot Instances are a cost-effective choice if you can be flexible about when your applications run and if your applications can be interrupted.
verified_claims: Amazon EC2 provides a Spot Instance interruption notice giving a two-minute warning before interruption.
An EC2 instance rebalance recommendation signals elevated interruption risk before the two-minute notice.
Spot Instances are not covered by Savings Plans, and Spot spend does not apply to Compute Savings Plans commitments.

core_services.name: EC2 Reserved Instances
core_services.job: Applies a billing discount to matching On-Demand usage in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment.
core_services.choose_when: You know a specific instance configuration will run steadily for the whole term.
core_services.avoid_when: Usage is unpredictable or the architecture is about to change; consider Savings Plans instead.
core_services.trap_words: unpredictable spikes, short-term projects, physical instances
core_services.aws_official_description: Reserved Instances are not physical instances, but rather a billing discount applied to the use of On-Demand Instances in your account that match certain attributes, such as instance type and Region.
verified_claims: Terms are one year (31536000 seconds) or three years (94608000 seconds), with three years discounting more.
Standard Reserved Instances discount most but can only be modified; Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged.
Zonal Reserved Instances reserve capacity in an Availability Zone; regional Reserved Instances do not.
AWS recommends Savings Plans over Reserved Instances, offering up to 72% off On-Demand pricing.

core_services.name: EC2 Placement Groups
core_services.job: Influences how interdependent EC2 instances are placed on the underlying hardware.
core_services.choose_when: You need HPC-style low-latency node-to-node networking, or strict separation across distinct hardware.
core_services.avoid_when: Ordinary web tiers already spread across Availability Zones by Auto Scaling.
core_services.trap_words: multi-Region placement, automatic scaling
core_services.aws_official_description: To meet the needs of your workload, you can launch a group of interdependent EC2 instances into a placement group to influence their placement.
verified_claims: Strategies are cluster, partition, spread, and precision time.
Cluster packs instances close together inside a single Availability Zone for low-latency HPC networking.
Spread strictly places a small group of instances on distinct underlying hardware to reduce correlated failures.
There is no charge for creating a placement group, and an instance can belong to only one at a time.

core_services.name: AWS CloudFormation
core_services.job: Models and provisions AWS resources from declarative JSON or YAML templates.
core_services.choose_when: You must reproduce a whole architecture consistently across Regions or accounts.
core_services.avoid_when: You only want to push application code into a managed environment.
core_services.trap_words: application code deployment, manual console clicking
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS CloudFormation is a service that helps you model and set up your AWS resources so that you can spend less time managing those resources and more time focusing on your applications.
verified_claims: You describe resources in a template, and CloudFormation provisions and configures them as a stack.
There is no additional charge for CloudFormation with AWS resource types; you pay for the resources created.
StackSets extend stacks across multiple accounts and Regions from a single template.

comparisons: Spot vs On-Demand: Spot uses spare capacity at a lower price but can be interrupted with a two-minute notice. On-Demand runs until you stop it at a static hourly price.
Reserved Instances vs Savings Plans: Reserved Instances commit to an instance configuration. Savings Plans commit to hourly spend and cover more instance families; AWS recommends them first.
Elastic Beanstalk vs CloudFormation: Beanstalk is a managed application platform that provisions environments for you. CloudFormation is generic infrastructure as code for any resource type.
Cluster vs spread placement group: cluster packs instances in one Availability Zone for low latency. Spread separates a small number of instances onto distinct hardware.
exam_moves: Interruptible batch, big data, or rendering work maps to EC2 Spot Instances for cost optimization.
Recreating an identical multi-tier stack in a second Region is a CloudFormation task.
A cluster placement group cannot span Availability Zones; a spread placement group can.
Uploading a Node.js app and letting AWS run the servers and load balancer points to Elastic Beanstalk.
Reserved Instances are a billing construct; only zonal Reserved Instances also reserve capacity.

core_services.name: Auto Scaling Groups (ASG)
core_services.job: Keeps a collection of EC2 instances between a minimum and maximum size and replaces unhealthy instances.
core_services.choose_when: You need elastic capacity and self-healing across multiple Availability Zones.
core_services.avoid_when: The application is a single stateful node that cannot scale horizontally.
core_services.trap_words: vertical scaling, stateful monolith
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling helps you ensure that you have the correct number of Amazon EC2 instances available to handle the load for your application, organized into collections called Auto Scaling groups.
verified_claims: EC2 Auto Scaling balances instances evenly across the Availability Zones you specify as the group scales.
There are no additional fees for EC2 Auto Scaling; you pay only for the resources used.
A single group can mix instance types and both Spot and On-Demand purchase options.
Instance refresh updates instances in a rolling fashion after you change the AMI or launch template.

core_services.name: Launch Templates
core_services.job: Stores versioned launch parameters such as AMI, instance type, security groups, and user data.
core_services.choose_when: You define what an Auto Scaling group or fleet should launch and want version control.
core_services.avoid_when: You are defining scaling policies, which live on the Auto Scaling group.
core_services.trap_words: scaling policies, CloudWatch alarms
core_services.aws_official_description: A launch template contains the configuration information to launch an instance, letting you store launch parameters so that you do not have to specify them every time you launch an instance.
verified_claims: Launch templates support versioning; each version is immutable and you create a new version to change parameters.
AWS recommends launch templates over launch configurations, which do not receive new EC2 features.

core_services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
core_services.job: Collects metrics and logs and raises alarms that can trigger scaling actions or notifications.
core_services.choose_when: You need metric-driven automation, dashboards, or threshold alerts on AWS resources.
core_services.avoid_when: You need an audit trail of who called which API, which is AWS CloudTrail.
core_services.trap_words: API auditing, who did what
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon CloudWatch monitors your Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources and the applications you run on AWS in real time, collecting and tracking metrics for your resources and applications.
verified_claims: CloudWatch alarms watch a single metric and can perform actions such as sending an Amazon SNS notification.
EC2 basic monitoring delivers metrics at 5-minute periods; detailed monitoring delivers them every 1 minute.

core_services.name: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
core_services.job: Distributes incoming traffic across healthy targets in one or more Availability Zones.
core_services.choose_when: You need traffic spread across a fleet with health checks and automatic registration of new instances.
core_services.avoid_when: You need routing across AWS Regions, which is Route 53 or Global Accelerator.
core_services.trap_words: cross-Region routing, DNS failover
core_services.aws_official_description: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes your incoming traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses, in one or more Availability Zones, and monitors the health of its registered targets.
verified_claims: ELB offers Application, Network, Gateway, and Classic Load Balancers.
Instances launched by an Auto Scaling group are automatically registered with the target group, and terminated ones are deregistered.

comparisons: Launch template vs launch configuration: templates are versioned and support current EC2 features such as mixed instance types. Launch configurations are legacy and receive no new features.
Step scaling vs target tracking: step scaling applies defined adjustments per alarm breach size. Target tracking adds or removes capacity to hold a metric near a target value.
Scheduled vs predictive scaling: scheduled scaling acts at times you specify. Predictive scaling forecasts load from historical data and provisions ahead of it.
exam_moves: To change an Auto Scaling group's instance type, create a new launch template version and point the group at it.
For a known, time-bound traffic spike, use scheduled scaling instead of waiting on reactive alarms.
Auto Scaling balances instances evenly across enabled Availability Zones, so scale-in favours the zone with the most instances.
Attach the Auto Scaling group to a target group so new instances are registered with the load balancer automatically.

Capping Lambda concurrency to protect a downstream database.
Compute Savings Plans cover EC2, Fargate, and Lambda for a 1- or 3-year hourly commitment.

signal_words.phrase: run code without provisioning or managing servers
event-driven code execution
prevent overwhelming a downstream database
eliminate cold start latency
discount spanning EC2, Fargate, and Lambda

core_services.name: AWS Lambda
core_services.job: Runs event-driven code with no servers to manage. Billed per request plus GB-seconds.
core_services.choose_when: Code must fire on an S3 upload, DynamoDB stream, SQS message, or API call.
core_services.avoid_when: One invocation runs over 15 minutes, needs over 10,240 MB, or needs persistent state.
core_services.trap_words: long-running processes, SSH access, persistent state
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service. You run code without provisioning or managing servers. Lambda manages the underlying infrastructure, including server maintenance, capacity provisioning, scaling, and patching.
verified_claims: Max 15 minutes (900 s) per invocation; max 10,240 MB memory.
Memory 128 MB to 10,240 MB in 1-MB steps. 1,769 MB equals one vCPU.
Default concurrent executions quota: 1,000 per Region. Increasable to tens of thousands.

core_services.name: Lambda reserved concurrency
core_services.job: Sets both the maximum and minimum concurrent instances for one function.
core_services.choose_when: A scaling function is exhausting connections on a downstream relational database.
core_services.avoid_when: You want to remove cold starts. That is provisioned concurrency, and it costs extra.
core_services.trap_words: prevent cold starts, pre-warmed environments
core_services.aws_official_description: Reserved concurrency sets both the maximum and minimum number of concurrent instances allocated to your function. No other function can use that concurrency. It can limit concurrency to prevent overwhelming downstream resources, like database connections.
verified_claims: Reserved concurrency is free. Provisioned concurrency incurs additional charges.
You can reserve up to unreserved account concurrency minus 100.
Reserved concurrency of 0 throttles the function completely.

core_services.name: Compute Savings Plans
core_services.job: Discounts compute for a committed hourly spend over 1 or 3 years.
core_services.choose_when: Steady compute spend spans Lambda, Fargate, and EC2 across families and Regions.
core_services.avoid_when: Usage is spiky, short-lived, or interruption-tolerant. Use On-Demand or Spot.
core_services.trap_words: instance-family lock-in, Region lock-in
core_services.aws_official_description: Savings Plans provide savings beyond On-Demand rates in exchange for committing to a specified amount of compute power per hour for one or three years. Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda usage.
verified_claims: Terms are 1 year (365 days) or 3 years (1,095 days).
AWS states savings of up to 72% on compute workloads.
Compute Savings Plans apply regardless of instance family, size, OS, tenancy, or Region.

comparisons: Lambda vs EC2: Lambda caps at 15 minutes and 10,240 MB; AWS patches and scales it. EC2 runs indefinitely but you patch it and scale with Auto Scaling groups.
Reserved vs provisioned concurrency: reserved caps scaling and is free. Provisioned pre-initializes environments to cut cold starts and costs extra.
Lambda vs API Gateway limits: Lambda defaults to 1,000 concurrent executions per Region. API Gateway's default request throttle is far higher, so Lambda throttles first.
exam_moves: 'Least operational overhead' plus a short event-driven task means Lambda.
Lambda exhausting RDS connections is fixed with reserved concurrency.
To reach a private RDS instance, attach the function to private subnets and security groups.
Attaching a function to a VPC removes its default internet access until you add a NAT path.
A discount that must cover Lambda and Fargate is Compute Savings Plans, not Reserved Instances.

what_this_tests: ECS is AWS-native orchestration. EKS is managed, Kubernetes-conformant.
Fargate is the serverless capacity option. No EC2 clusters to provision or scale.
API Gateway fronts REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs with auth, throttling, and usage plans.

signal_words.phrase: run containers without managing servers or clusters of EC2 instances
AWS-native container orchestration
Kubernetes, kubectl, CNCF-conformant
publish, throttle, and secure APIs at any scale
interruption-tolerant containers at a discount

core_services.name: AWS Fargate
core_services.job: Serverless capacity for ECS and EKS. You never provision, configure, or scale EC2 clusters.
core_services.choose_when: Containers must run with minimum operational overhead. You supply CPU, memory, networking, IAM.
core_services.avoid_when: You need host OS access, GPUs or specific CPU architectures, or unsupported task parameters.
core_services.trap_words: managing worker nodes, host OS access, GPU instances
core_services.aws_official_description: AWS Fargate runs containers with Amazon ECS without managing servers or clusters of EC2 instances. You no longer provision, configure, or scale clusters of virtual machines to run containers.
verified_claims: Each Fargate task has its own isolation boundary. It shares no kernel, CPU, memory, or ENI with another task.
Fargate Spot runs interruption-tolerant ECS tasks on spare capacity with a two-minute warning.
Fargate tasks use awsvpc networking, so load balancer target groups must use target type 'ip'.

core_services.name: Amazon EKS
core_services.job: Managed Kubernetes. AWS runs the control plane; EKS Auto Mode also runs the nodes.
core_services.choose_when: You must keep Kubernetes APIs, manifests, and community tooling.
core_services.avoid_when: There is no Kubernetes requirement. Use ECS.
core_services.trap_words: simplest container management, no Kubernetes requirement
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon EKS is a fully managed Kubernetes service. With EKS standard, AWS manages the Kubernetes control plane when you create a cluster.
verified_claims: EKS is certified Kubernetes-conformant. Kubernetes-compatible apps deploy without refactoring.
EKS Auto Mode provisions infrastructure, scales resources, and patches node operating systems.
EKS charges per cluster. You pay separately for EC2, EBS, and other node resources.

core_services.name: Amazon ECS
core_services.job: AWS-native managed orchestrator for containers across Fargate, EC2, Managed Instances, and on-premises.
core_services.choose_when: You want deep AWS integration and no Kubernetes control plane.
core_services.avoid_when: The scenario requires Kubernetes APIs or cross-cloud manifest portability.
core_services.trap_words: multi-cloud portability, Kubernetes APIs, kubectl
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon ECS is a fully managed container orchestration service that deploys, manages, and scales containerized applications, with AWS configuration and operational best practices built in.
verified_claims: Capacity options: Fargate, EC2 instances you manage, ECS Managed Instances, and ECS Anywhere on-premises.
Core objects: task definition, cluster, task, service.
ECS provides Cluster Auto Scaling for EC2 capacity and Service Auto Scaling for task count.

core_services.name: Amazon API Gateway
core_services.job: Managed front door for REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at any scale.
core_services.choose_when: Lambda or backend services need HTTP endpoints with auth, throttling, API keys, and canary deploys.
core_services.avoid_when: You only need internal VPC load balancing. Use an ALB, or Cloud Map for discovery.
core_services.trap_words: internal load balancing, container hosting
core_services.aws_official_description: Amazon API Gateway creates, publishes, maintains, monitors, and secures REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at any scale. It acts as a front door to backend services.
verified_claims: Supports stateful WebSocket APIs and stateless HTTP and REST APIs.
Throttles with a token bucket (rate plus burst) and returns 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded.
Per-client limits come from API keys in usage plans. Integrates with AWS WAF and X-Ray.

comparisons: ECS vs EKS: ECS is AWS's own orchestrator with AWS best practices built in. EKS is certified Kubernetes-conformant and required when the question says Kubernetes.
Fargate vs EC2 launch type: Fargate means no EC2 clusters to provision, configure, or scale. EC2 launch type means you pick instance types and manage capacity.
API Gateway vs ALB: API Gateway adds auth, usage plans, API keys, throttling, and canary releases. An ALB is a layer 7 load balancer only.
exam_moves: 'Run containers with least operational overhead' means Fargate capacity, on ECS or EKS.
Any mention of Kubernetes or kubectl selects EKS over ECS.
Per-client API rate limits mean API Gateway usage plans with API keys, not a custom EC2 proxy.
Interruption-tolerant container batch work at lower cost is Fargate Spot.
